name: Avalon City
summary: The burned seat of Albion's learning on the Shrouded Isles, occupied by five drakoran clans who have taken up the trades of the city they destroyed.

facts.text: Morgana, seeking all of Arthur's former lands, allied with the drakoran, dragon-men said to be led by a huge dragon. They devastated Avalon Isle and its capital, Albion's centre of learning, and drove out its people.
Avalon City is a largely destroyed dungeon for levels 35-50; Arawn leads the Inconnu to reclaim it.

In Mythic's Catacombs lore Morgana trapped Merlin in a crystal in a cave of converging ley lines and attacked Avalon with the drakoran horde; Arawn's forces are stretched by his war against the drakoran in Avalon.

The drakoran of the city come in five clans whose names echo their lords': drau'gyn (Dra'argus), dry'ak (Dura'ek), syhr'phint (Sys'sro), vyr'em (Vera'erius) and wi'voron (Weno'iak); the lords' linked packs are of their own clan. The clan reading is inferred from names and packs.
Their ranks carry old English trade names: reeve, sutler, joyner, lorimer, tranter, catchpole, stallman, acater, halberdier, alblaster.

Players in January 2003 described a named near the Crystal Cave entrance, by the flamethrowers, who could not be struck until a great flaming orb upstairs was destroyed; an October 2004 reply named him Dra'argus the Mighty.
No period raid count was found for Dura'ek; the raid is sized like Krondon.
Existing bot chat says the drakoran have mystics, medics and sawbones, and asks who empowered Dura'ek.
Albion bot chat: the old guides said the marsh ran right up to the edges of Avalon City; the drakoran have mystics, medics and sawbones.

story:
Avalon was the city where Albion kept its learning. Its colleges stood on the isle across the water from the marsh, and the old guides said the marsh ran right up to its edges, because the scholars of Avalon had made the water forget it was there. Merlin was taught there. So was Morgana.

When she came back it was at the head of the drakoran, the dragon-men, who are said to follow a dragon of their own, and the city burned. The libraries burned first. The colleges came down, the people fled to Caer Gothwaite and the Isle of Glass, and the drakoran did not leave. That is the strangest thing about Avalon City: it is not a ruin. It is occupied. Five clans of drakoran hold its quarters, each under its own lord, and they have taken up the trades of the city they destroyed. There are drakoran reeves and sutlers, joiners and lorimers, catchpoles to keep order and acaters to buy in the stores, physicians and stall-keepers, as if a city were a coat they could put on.

Dura'ek the Empowered rules them all from the heart of the city, and the clans whisper that his power is not his own. Under the city, past the sentries who bear the dragon's name, a way leads down to the Crystal Cave, where something with two heads sleeps on a mound of light. The Inconnu fight in these streets for Arawn. Albion fights in them for its memory. The drakoran fight in them because they live here now.

The colleges. Avalon was never a city of soldiers. It was a city of readers, built on its isle across the water from the marsh by scholars who had learned to make the water forget it was there, so that the marsh seemed to run right up to the city's edges and a traveller could walk to the colleges dry-shod at dusk. It had a college for every art: for the stars, for the law, for the old tongues of the isles, for healing, for the magic that Merlin would one day carry to Camelot. Merlin read there as a boy. So did a girl called Morgana, Arthur's sister, the quickest pupil the readers ever had.

The burning. When Morgana came back she knew where the libraries were, and the drakoran burned them first. The readers watched from their boats as the colleges came down one by one, and on the third night they saw a light rise out of the ground at the heart of the city, cold and many-coloured, as if the earth there were glass. They fled to Caer Gothwaite on the Isle of Glass behind the earthen wall and the three ring-forts, and they have not been home since. Some of them think the light was Xanxicar waking. Some think it was Merlin's own crystal, brought here. Nobody has gone down to check and come back with an answer.

The occupation. The drakoran did not leave. Five clans of them hold the city's quarters, each under its own lord, and they live as citizens of the place they burned. The drau'gyn, Dra'argus's clan, keep the flamethrowers and the tall burned college by the way down. The dry'ak, Dura'ek's clan, are its halberdiers and doorkeepers and hold the chancellors' court at the heart. The syhr'phint, Sys'sro's clan, are taskers and catchpoles and keep order in the streets and the pit in the cloister garden. The vyr'em, Vera'erius's clan, are the swordsmen. The wi'voron, Weno'iak's clan, are reeves and advisors and the cavalry who stamp in the colleges' yards. Between them they keep a city: reeves and sutlers, joiners and lorimers, tranters and stall-keepers, physicians in the old hospital. Under the heart of it all, Xanxicarian sentries hold the way down to the Crystal Cave.

Why it matters. Avalon is Albion's memory, and it is occupied by the people who burned it. Arawn's Inconnu fight in its streets because Morgana steals his dead. Albion fights in them because its learning lies under the ashes, and because whatever rose out of the ground on the third night is still down there. The old readers in Caer Gothwaite still keep a list of the colleges, in order, so that someone will know which ruin was which on the day the city is taken back.
legend: Every lord in Avalon City has a trick, and every trick has killed a raid, and the Albion guilds who raided it in 2003 learned them the hard way. Dra'argus cannot be hurt until you break the great flaming orb upstairs in his house, and players were puzzling that out at the turn of the year. Dura'ek drinks fire and frost, so leave the wizards on his avowries. Vera'erius drinks body and spirit. Sys'sro throws you into his pit with fifteen beasts. Weno'iak rides with sixteen horsemen and their steeds. The city is a thousand mobs deep, so raids move street by street, and the drakoran sneaks at the back entrance con red to anyone under forty. The old guides said the marsh ran right to the city's edges; nobody has ever found those edges. The readers of Caer Gothwaite still keep a list of the colleges, and some raiders carry a copy so they know which ruin they are standing in. Never call it a ruin to an old reader. They say it is only occupied.

firstEntry: Avalon burned. The drakoran live in the ashes now.
The libraries are gone. Dragon-men keep the streets.
Ash on the cobbles. The colleges are gone.

A city of readers, kept by those who burned it.

loremaster.intro: Avalon was Albion's seat of learning, and [Morgana] burned it. The [drakoran] did not leave. Five clans hold it now under five lords, and the greatest of them is [Dura'ek].

topics.morgana: Merlin's own pupil, taught in Avalon's colleges. She came back at the head of the dragon-men, and the libraries burned first. Arawn sent his Inconnu to fight her here, for she steals his dead.
topics.drakoran: Dragon-men, and no beasts. They have reeves and sutlers, joiners and physicians, catchpoles and stall-keepers. Five clans, each under a lord: [Dra'argus], Dura'ek, [Sys'sro], [Vera'erius] and [Weno'iak]. They are said to follow a dragon of their own. Ask about the [Crystal Cave].
topics.dura'ek: The Empowered. He rules the city from its heart, and fire and frost only feed him. The clans whisper that his power is not his own. I think they are right, and I think I know whose it is.
topics.dra'argus: The Mighty, lord of the drau'gyn and their flamethrowers. He cannot be wounded while the great orb in his house burns. Break the orb.
topics.sys'sro: The Ruthless. Fifteen beasts live in his pit, and he throws men into it. Keep your back to the wall.
topics.vera'erius: The Brave. Spirit and body magic heal him, and when he is hurt he heals himself. Bring steel.
topics.weno'iak: The Enlightened. His clan rides warsteeds, and he burns men with a light that is not fire.
topics.crystal cave: Under the heart of the city a way goes down, guarded by sentries who carry the name Xanxicarian. At the bottom sleeps a dragon with two heads. I do not think the drakoran found him. I think he called them.
topics.colleges: Avalon had a college for every art: stars, law, healing, the old tongues, the magic Merlin carried to Camelot. The readers of Caer Gothwaite keep their list in order, against the day the city is retaken.
topics.readers: The scholars of Avalon who fled by boat to Caer Gothwaite. They watched the burning, and on the third night they saw a light rise from the city's heart. Ask about the [crystal cave].
topics.clans: Drau'gyn of [Dra'argus], dry'ak of [Dura'ek], syhr'phint of [Sys'sro], vyr'em of [Vera'erius], wi'voron of [Weno'iak]. Each clan keeps its quarter and its trade.
topics.third night: On the third night of the burning a cold, many-coloured light rose out of the ground at the city's heart. Some readers say Xanxicar woke. Some say Merlin's crystal was brought there. No one has gone to see and returned.
topics.inconnu: Arawn's servants, who fight in Avalon's streets because Morgana steals their lord's dead. Albion's knights fight beside them, uneasily.

book.title: What the Scholars Left
pages: What the Scholars Left, set down at Caer Gothwaite by Elowen, last of the readers of the college of the old tongues, so that something of us is written somewhere. Our city stood across the water from the marsh, and the marsh ran right to its edges, for our masters had made the water forget it was there. We had a college for every art. Merlin read with us as a boy. So did the girl who came back. We taught her well. That is the whole of our shame, and it is enough. I set down here the colleges in their order, so that someone will know.

She did not come alone. She came with the dragon-men, and they burned the libraries first, because she knew where they were; she had read in every one of them. We fled by boat. From the water we watched the colleges come down one by one: the stars on the first night, the law and the healing on the second. On the third night we saw something we have not been able to explain, a light rising out of the ground at the heart of the city, cold and many-coloured, as if the earth itself were made of glass. Our master of stars wept. I did not know why until much later.

Our fishermen go close sometimes. They say the dragon-men did not leave. They live in our houses. They have reeves and sutlers and joiners, catchpoles who keep order in our streets, physicians who tend their wounded in our hospital. There are five clans of them, each with a lord, and the clans have taken our quarters as if by lot: the flame-carriers have the tall college by the way down, the halberdiers have the chancellors' court, the catchpoles the cloister, the swordsmen the old schools, the riders the yards. They are not beasts. That is the worst of it. They are citizens.

The greatest lord sits in the court of our chancellors and is called the Empowered. My fishermen say his own people do not believe the power is his. One of them saw a wizard of the Inconnu throw fire at him in the street and watched the drakoran lord stand in the flame and grow stronger. Frost the same. Steel, the fisherman said, steel he did not like at all. I have written to Camelot about steel. Camelot has written back that it is aware of steel. I think they are not yet aware of what is under the court.

One fisherman went closer than the rest and came back with a word he had heard the guards say over and over, as soldiers say the name of their king: Xanxicar. We have looked for it in what books we saved. It is in none of them. But the oldest map of Avalon in our possession, drawn before the colleges were built, marks the heart of the isle with a small drawing of a beast with two heads, and no name at all. Our master of stars said, when he saw it, that we had built our city on a lid.

The Inconnu come to Caer Gothwaite sometimes, pale and quiet, to speak with the knights. I asked one of them what his lord wanted with our city. He said his lord wanted nothing with our city; his lord wanted the witch, who steals the dead, and the witch's friends were in our city, and so his people would fight there until the witch had no friends. I asked him whether the city would be ours again afterwards. He looked at me for a long time and said that the dead do not keep cities, and that I should keep my list.
